sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The ball and the notch are unresponsive. The only interactive element is the T glyph.
Let me think about the T glyph from a different angle. What if the T glyph is a "lock" that controls a row of the checkerboard? There are 5 glyphs, and the board has 7 rows of tiles. Or maybe it controls a column? There are 8 columns.
Or, the T glyph might be a "score" that increases when the piece is dropped, and my toggling might have been a mistake (though the board did change).
Wait, actually—maybe I should reconsider. When I clicked T3 and T1, the glyph changed from B to w. But maybe that wasn't a "toggle"—maybe it was a "consumption": the dark T was a "button," and clicking it consumed it (it became a used/light state). In other words, the dark T is a "button," and the light T is "used." Initially there were 2 dark buttons (T1, T3) and 3 light ones (T2, T4, T5). I consumed both of the dark buttons. And nothing happened on the board.
Hmm, so what do the dark buttons do? Nothing visible.
Let me try clicking the light T glyph (T2, col 26) and see if it toggles to dark (i.e., if it's a full toggle) or if it does nothing (i.e., if the light one is inert).

    return [r for r in range(min(len(pa),len(ca))) if pa[r] != ca[r]]
res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':44,'col':26}])
r = diff_rows(previous_frame, current_frame)

res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':44,'col':31}])

</parameter>
</function>
